title: satisfies, as and an annotation around a local value, and satisfies and a parenthesis around trusted foreign callees, introduce no boundary refusal and the program runs
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Foreign Boundary': 'Calling an unannotated foreign runtime value MUST add the checked panic case ... Trusted @throws {never} metadata opts out.' Nothing in this program is an unannotated foreign call: three of the seven lines wrap a LOCAL object and four reach declarations that carry the marker. So all seven must compile, and all seven must run. WHY THIS CASE EXISTS: it is the over-correction guard for the whole `satisfies` family. The refusal cases beside it require a rule that looks THROUGH `satisfies`, `as` and an annotation to find a foreign declaration, and the cheap way to satisfy them is to refuse anything with a type-only operator anywhere near it. This repository has shipped seven over-corrections, and one of the two defects this family closed on 2026-08-27 was in exactly that direction: the fork refused a trusted foreign callee reached through `satisfies` that the reference accepted. That line is here (`trustedCalleeThroughSatisfies`), and it prints `4`. THE OUTPUT IS THE EVIDENCE, not a formality. A refusal case proves a program was rejected; only running proves the accepted program still does what it says. `double(2)` is `4` and `double(3)` is `6`, so the two trusted-callee lines print values that came back across the foreign boundary; `trustedTag` joins its raw strings, so `a` is the tag's own return and not a fallback; `giveString` returns `s`. A backend that accepted these and lowered them to nothing would print blanks and the case would go red. THE THREE LOCAL LINES ARE NOT FILLER: they are the control that says the four foreign ones are clean because their declarations are TRUSTED and not because the wrappers are ignored — a rule that ignored `satisfies` entirely would also pass the local lines, so the two halves together are what identify the cause. `trustedCalleeParenthesised` is the parenthesis spelling of the same question, kept because a parenthesised callee is a separate table entry on both backends and has diverged before. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: a trusted foreign value RETURNED out of a `.sm` function. That is a different rule (`SMITHERS1508`, escaping provenance) with its own cases, and every value here is a `number` or a `string` that has already left the boundary. It also does not pin `as` around a FOREIGN trusted declaration, which erases the marker and is refused — that is `an-as-or-an-annotation-erases-a-trust-marker-where-satisfies-does-not`, and keeping the two apart means neither case's green depends on the other's rule. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the fourth declared stdout line from `4` to `5` — the trusted-callee-through-`satisfies` line, the one whose acceptance was the fork's over-refusal — turns the case red on BOTH backends with the stdout diff printed, and the expectation was restored byte-identically (sha256 f1482c891ac12014ab4f335483662c244580d89b023a96873c04e9441f07ed84 before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently).
